license: BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE; w3lib and Protego, read as dependencies, are BSD-3-Clause)
method: Pinned checkout in an isolated scratch directory and an isolated virtualenv with Scrapy 2.19.0 (this commit), w3lib 2.5.0 and Protego 0.7.0 installed from it. Source read for the behaviours below; the donor's own code was then run as a frozen oracle against ECDEV on bounded cases (URL identity, redirects, robots, cache freshness, retry, gzip) and the results pinned in tests. No donor code is copied into ECDEV and Scrapy is not a runtime or test dependency; the oracles are generated by tools/commerce/scrapy_*_oracle.py and committed as fixtures. Live behaviour was measured only through ECDEV's own robots-respecting runtime or on robots.txt files and published sitemaps.
licence_note: Scrapy is BSD-3-Clause. No legal conclusion is made.

read: scrapy/pqueues.py (priority and downloader-aware queues; storage classes skimmed)
scrapy/core/engine.py (stop and close entry points only)
not_read: scrapy/core/downloader/handlers other than http11 (aiohttp, httpx, ftp, s3, file, datauri, base)
scrapy/downloadermiddlewares (defaultheaders, downloadtimeout beyond its meta key, httpauth, httpproxy, jsonvalidation, stats, useragent)
scrapy/extensions other than throttle, httpcache and closespider (17 files)
scrapy/loader, scrapy/selector, scrapy/pipelines (files, images, media), scrapy/exporters.py, scrapy/mail.py
scrapy/spidermiddlewares/referer.py and base.py, scrapy/spiders other than sitemap
scrapy/utils (about 49 other files, including url.py, response.py, python.py, defer.py, request helpers)
docs, extras, conftest and project templates
coverage.statement: About 26 of 209 first-party source files were read for behaviour. This is a bounded review of the acquisition-relevant core, not a whole-source semantic census; semantic_review stays below COMPLETE and no extinction or cutover is claimed.

rows.behaviour: SHA-1 over JSON of method, canonical URL, body (hex) and selected request headers (hex); the fragment is dropped unless keep_fragments; the canonical URL sorts query pairs, keeps blank values, resolves dot segments, normalises percent escapes, lowercases the host, and does not strip an explicit default port. Cached per request.
rows.configuration: REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_CLASS; include_headers, keep_fragments arguments; meta verbatim_url skips canonicalisation
rows.ecdev_today: adapter/domain frontier::canonicalize: SHA-256 over the canonical URL only (ECDEV sends credentialless GETs, so method, body and headers carry no identity); WHATWG URL parsing; query order, a bare '?' and tracking parameters are significant unless a policy asks; escapes uppercased and unreserved decoded; URL length bounded at 8,192 bytes
rows.ecdev_real_caller: yes: research crawl, monitor targets, robots URL (all with the default policy)
rows.runtime_decision: not executed; ECDEV's identity is native
rows.knowledge: ECDEV and Scrapy merge host case, scheme case, dot segments, an empty path, fragments, escaped unreserved letters and escape case, and keep path case, parameter values and names apart. They differ in three named ways: ECDEV merges an explicit default port (Scrapy fetches ':443' and the bare URL as two requests); query order and a bare trailing '?' are distinct by default in ECDEV and merged by Scrapy; tracking parameters are never removed by Scrapy and only by ECDEV policy.
rows.evidence: domain/commerce/tests/scrapy_url_identity.rs over 569 frozen rewrites of 616 real URLs from live captures (tools/commerce/scrapy_url_identity_oracle.py; Scrapy 2.19.0 at 54f7ed9c, w3lib 2.5.0); research/commerce/scrapy-semantic-review.json
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answered: frozen oracle compared and pinned

rows.donor_source: w3lib.url.canonicalize_url (query sort, blank values, keep_fragments) as used by scrapy/utils/request.py and scrapy/linkextractors/lxmlhtml.py (unique=True)
rows.behaviour: Always sorts query pairs and drops a bare '?', so links differing only by parameter order are one request.
rows.ecdev_today: frontier::UrlPolicy has sort_query, collapse_slashes, tracking_parameters, identity_parameters, all off by default; no production caller turns them on
rows.ecdev_real_caller: no: every production caller passes UrlPolicy::default()
rows.knowledge: whether turning on query sorting and tracking-parameter removal for crawl discovery would merge any real duplicate links, on link sets from tracking-heavy sites (affiliate and newsletter navigation): measured on 8 saved pages (2,586 links) and 646 post URLs it merged zero, and a bare trailing '?' occurred in 0 of 1,703 page links
rows.evidence: measurement in this wave: 1,703 page links on 7 pages, 0 merged by sorting, 0 by a tracking list (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, ref...), 1 link with a tracking parameter; sample too small and too editorial to close the question
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: open: needs link sets from sites with tracking-parameter navigation

rows.behaviour: A fingerprint set; request_seen() adds a fingerprint the first time it is asked, at enqueue, and appends it to requests.seen at once when JOBDIR is set (or writes a SQLite row for DiskDupeFilter); dont_filter bypasses it; the first duplicate is logged, later ones counted.
rows.failure_semantics: A request is 'seen' before it is done: a request in flight at a crash is already recorded as seen and no longer in the queue, so a resumed crawl neither re-queues it nor lets the spider re-enqueue it (from reading the source; not executed).
rows.ecdev_today: frontier crawl_urls keyed by (run, identity_hash) with states PENDING, LEASED, RETRYABLE, HANDLED, FAILED, CANCELLED; an expired lease returns the URL to RETRYABLE
rows.knowledge: ECDEV records progress, not mere sight: a discovered URL is distinct from a leased one and from a handled one, and an expired lease is reclaimed. Scrapy's seen-at-enqueue rule is cheaper and can lose in-flight work on a crash.
rows.evidence: domain/commerce/tests/frontier.rs (lease expiry and reclaim); source reading of dupefilters.py and scheduler.py
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answerable by a crash-injection test of Scrapy; not built (source reading only)

rows.behaviour: Priority buckets of queues; LIFO by default (depth-first) in memory and on disk, FIFO for start requests; the default queue picks the download slot with the fewest active requests and breaks ties round-robin after the last choice; a request that cannot be serialised falls back to the memory queue.
rows.failure_semantics: unserialisable requests are counted and kept in memory only, so they do not survive a restart
rows.ecdev_today: frontier::lease: ORDER BY priority DESC, next_at, discovered_at, rowid (FIFO within a priority, so breadth-first), among URLs whose origin is not cooling down and has fewer leases than per_origin_concurrency; global_concurrency, max_pages and deadline bound a run
rows.knowledge: Breadth-first by design (ECDEV researches a site's neighbourhood to a depth, not an unbounded descent); origin fairness comes from the cooldown and per-origin lease cap, so a large queue for one origin does not starve another.
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: ordering equivalence is not a goal; no oracle

rows.behaviour: With JOBDIR the disk queue, the active priority list and the seen file persist; state is written at close and every JOBDIR_SYNC_EVERY changes.
rows.failure_semantics: A kill between syncs loses the unsynced queue state; requests being downloaded are in neither the queue nor the next run.
rows.ecdev_today: SQLite frontier with Immediate transactions, fenced lease tokens and reclaim; cancel and deadline are states
rows.knowledge: ECDEV's durable frontier makes crash recovery a state transition (an expired lease is observable and reclaimed) rather than a file sync.
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answerable by crash injection; not built

rows.behaviour: Retries a fixed list of statuses (500, 502, 503, 504, 522, 524, 408, 429) and a list of exceptions up to RETRY_TIMES (2), re-queueing a copy with dont_filter set and priority lowered by one; per-request meta overrides; no delay is added.
rows.failure_semantics: gives up with a log at RETRY_GIVE_UP_LOG_LEVEL after the limit; the response is returned when retries run out
rows.configuration: RETRY_ENABLED, RETRY_TIMES, RETRY_HTTP_CODES, RETRY_EXCEPTIONS, RETRY_PRIORITY_ADJUST, meta max_retry_times, dont_retry
rows.ecdev_today: research::retryable_failure decides; the frontier retries up to max_retries (at most 20) with exponential backoff capped at max_backoff_ms and an origin cooldown from Retry-After
rows.knowledge: Same transient statuses; Scrapy retries immediately at lower priority, ECDEV waits (backoff and Retry-After). Found by comparison and fixed: ECDEV did not retry 408 and did retry the permanent 501, 505 and 511.

rows.donor_source: searched all of scrapy/ for 'retry-after' and 'retry_after': no match
rows.behaviour: Scrapy does not read Retry-After at all: a 429 or 503 is retried by the generic rule with no delay beyond the download delay.
rows.failure_semantics: a rate-limited origin is hit again at once, at lower priority
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV propagates Retry-After (seconds or HTTP date) into AcquireError and the frontier's origin cooldown, and bounds it
rows.knowledge: A deliberate and proven divergence in ECDEV's favour: honouring Retry-After is a politeness requirement ECDEV has and Scrapy lacks.
rows.evidence: grep over the pinned source (zero matches); ECDEV tests in adapter/web and domain/commerce/tests/frontier.rs

rows.behaviour: Follows 301, 302, 303, 307, 308 with a Location, up to 20 hops (redirect_ttl), re-attaching the request's fragment; POST becomes GET on 301/302 and non-GET/HEAD becomes GET on 303; Cookie is dropped on a host change, Authorization on a scheme, host or port change; a Location that is not http(s) leaves the response as is; raises on an unparseable URL.
rows.failure_semantics: max redirections raises IgnoreRequest; an invalid URL raises ValueError
rows.configuration: REDIRECT_ENABLED, REDIRECT_MAX_TIMES (20), REDIRECT_PRIORITY_ADJUST (+2), meta dont_redirect, handle_httpstatus_list
rows.ecdev_today: adapter/web redirect_target(current, status, location): same statuses, public-URL policy on every target, a bounded hop limit; the fetch path now percent-encodes raw non-ASCII Location bytes as received instead of dropping them
rows.knowledge: Of 2,000 cases, 1,700 agree in decision and target. ECDEV refuses what Scrapy follows only where its policy says so (credentials in a target, a credential-named query parameter, non-http schemes) or where a Location is resolved differently by different clients ('//', '///x', 'http:/x', a host with a space, backslashes). Found and fixed: a non-ASCII Location (a Japanese path, an IDN host) was dropped as if absent, so the redirect read as the final response; ECDEV now follows it as Scrapy does.

rows.donor_source: scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/redirect.py::MetaRefreshMiddleware (the head of process_response was read; the HTML meta parsing in scrapy/utils/response.py was not)
rows.behaviour: Follows <meta http-equiv=refresh> in HTML responses up to METAREFRESH_MAXDELAY seconds, ignoring it inside script, noscript and similar tags.
rows.ecdev_today: not followed
rows.knowledge: how many store and listing pages redirect only by meta refresh, which ECDEV reads as a final page with no products
rows.evidence: 0 of 57 distinct HTML pages in this wave's captures carry a meta refresh; too few to estimate prevalence
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: open: needs a larger page sample

rows.behaviour: Off by default (ROBOTSTXT_OBEY = False). When on: fetches /robots.txt per netloc once per crawl at priority 1000 and parses whatever body comes back whatever the status; a download error means no parser, which allows everything; the user agent defaults to the request's.
rows.failure_semantics: fail-open on every error and on any status; a 5xx page is parsed as if it were robots rules; never refetched during a crawl
rows.ecdev_today: robots are consulted for every fetch; 404 allows, any other non-200 or unknown state refuses, a parse limit refuses; AI-agent refusals are honoured; Crawl-delay is honoured; cached with expiry
rows.knowledge: ECDEV is fail-closed and status-aware (RFC 9309); Scrapy is opt-in and fail-open. Not a gap to close.

rows.behaviour: Protego: longest-pattern-wins with Allow winning ties, '*' and '$' patterns, group merging, case-insensitive agent matching, tolerant parsing (missing colon, CR line ends), Crawl-delay.
rows.failure_semantics: decodes as utf-8-sig ignoring errors; an unparseable file is an empty file (allow all)
rows.ecdev_today: adapter/web/src/robots.rs evaluate: reppy-oracle parity on 1,620 cases plus the fixes below; invalid directives void the group (fail-closed)
rows.knowledge: ECDEV and Protego agree on all 1,620 reppy-oracle cases and on 37 of 47 handcrafted edge-case texts. Live, over 256 real robots.txt files and 5,499 URL checks the two differed in 3 files: google.com (ECDEV allowed what the file disallows: consecutive 'User-agent: *' and 'User-agent: Yandex' lines lost the wildcard group), monolog.r-n-i.jp ('Allow: /item/*' tied with 'Disallow: /item/' after ECDEV stripped the trailing wildcard) and cs.android.com ('Disallow: /*' tied with 'Allow: /$'). All three fixed; a bare-CR file was also read as one line, now fixed. One difference remains live: a 'User -agent' typo makes ECDEV refuse a site Protego allows (the cautious side). Recorded divergences: ECDEV applies rules written before any User-agent line to every agent, refuses a pattern given both Allow and Disallow, voids a group on an unparseable Crawl-delay or a '$' inside a pattern, and does not accept directives without a colon or substring agent names; none occurred in 247 live files.
rows.evidence: adapter/web/tests/scrapy_robots.rs (1,620 + 2,538 frozen Protego decisions; tools/commerce/scrapy_robots_oracle.py, scrapy_robots_probe.py); live comparison over 256 files recorded in research/commerce/ecdev-live-runtime-validation.json
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answered: oracle, probe and live corpus

rows.behaviour: Per download slot: target delay = latency / AUTOTHROTTLE_TARGET_CONCURRENCY; new delay = max(target, mean(old, target)), clamped to [DOWNLOAD_DELAY, AUTOTHROTTLE_MAX_DELAY]; a non-200 response cannot lower the delay.
rows.ecdev_today: fixed 750 ms minimum origin interval, per-origin lease cap (default serial), Retry-After cooldown, backoff on failure; per-request time-to-headers and body time are now recorded
rows.knowledge: does a latency-derived per-origin interval beat the fixed 750 ms floor, measured as origin response latency under ECDEV's own request pattern over a time series
rows.evidence: live, 12 origins through the operator proxy (2026-10-07): time-to-headers median 584 ms, max 1,190 ms; 5 of 12 above 750 ms. Serial per-origin leasing already holds target concurrency near 1, so the formula's main effect is already structural. One snapshot per origin cannot show whether latency rises under load.
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: open: needs a time series per origin

rows.behaviour: Slots keyed by hostname (or resolved IP); concurrency per slot (8) and total (16); delay with ±50% jitter by default; per-slot overrides; slot garbage collection.
rows.failure_semantics: downloader shutdown cancels queued downloads with DownloadCancelledError
rows.ecdev_today: per-origin (scheme, host, port) lease cap and interval from CrawlLimits; deterministic timing
rows.knowledge: ECDEV schedules deterministically (reproducible tests, auditable timing) and never randomises delay: jitter exists in Scrapy to look less mechanical, which is not a goal for a crawler that identifies itself and obeys robots.

rows.behaviour: RFC2616Policy: stores a response only with max-age, Expires, a permanent redirect status, or a validator; freshness lifetime is max-age, else Expires minus Date, else one tenth of the time since Last-Modified, else 0; current age is max(now minus Date, Age); no-cache and no-store respected; request-side max-age and max-stale honoured; a cached 5xx-era response is served stale on server error unless must-revalidate.
rows.ecdev_today: research::freshness_lifetime: RFC 9111 max-age, Expires minus Date, Age subtracted, no-store/no-cache give none, one-hour default, never past 24 hours; stale-if-error only when asked (allow_stale) and reported STALE_USABLE
rows.knowledge: Over 528 header combinations ECDEV and Scrapy give the same remaining freshness in 395; ECDEV holds a page at most 24 hours (96 cases where Scrapy keeps it longer), treats an invalid max-age as already stale (13), holds a response with no freshness information for its one-hour default (16) where Scrapy keeps nothing, and has no Last-Modified heuristic (8).

rows.behaviour: With only Last-Modified, a response stays fresh for a tenth of its age at fetch time.
rows.ecdev_today: not used; the default hour applies
rows.knowledge: does a Last-Modified heuristic cut refetches of rarely changing pages without serving a stale commerce fact, measured against the change rate ECDEV's own monitor observes
rows.evidence: 8 of 528 grid cases differ by it; no change-rate data to weigh it yet
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: open: needs monitor history on static pages

rows.behaviour: A stale cached response adds If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since from its own ETag and Last-Modified; a 304 revalidates it.
rows.ecdev_today: validators_for sends validators only to the URL whose response produced them and only on the first hop; an unsolicited 304 is refused (UNSOLICITED_NOT_MODIFIED); a 304 reuses the stored capture
rows.knowledge: Same mechanism; ECDEV is stricter about which URL a validator may reach.

rows.behaviour: A cookie jar per cookiejar key; cookies set on responses are sent back; cookie domains that are public suffixes are accepted only for the exact host.
rows.failure_semantics: invalid cookies are logged and skipped
rows.ecdev_today: no cookie jar: credentialless GET only; no session carried between requests
rows.knowledge: ECDEV acquires public pages without a session, so a region, price or availability that depends on a cookie is simply not observed, and says so (SOURCE_BLOCKED or absent fields), rather than being persisted into a session. The public-suffix cookie rule is the only fragment worth remembering.

rows.behaviour: Non-2xx responses are not passed to the spider unless allowed by status list or meta; the first is logged and counted.
rows.ecdev_today: every non-200 becomes a typed failure reason (HTTP_STATUS_nnn, UNSOLICITED_NOT_MODIFIED, ...) kept in the run's errors and provider calls
rows.knowledge: ECDEV keeps the failure as evidence (a 404 and a robots refusal are different findings); live survey of 36 hosts recorded 404, 204 and refusals by name.

rows.behaviour: DOWNLOAD_MAXSIZE (1 GiB) is checked against Content-Length before reading and enforced mid-stream; DOWNLOAD_WARNSIZE (32 MiB) warns; DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT 180 s.
rows.ecdev_today: 4 MiB body cap, 20 s request timeout; found and fixed: a declared Content-Length past the cap is now refused before the body is read
rows.knowledge: Same two-stage check, much tighter bounds.

rows.behaviour: Sends Accept-Encoding gzip, deflate, br, zstd; decodes encodings stacked in order; every decoder stops at DOWNLOAD_MAXSIZE of decoded output (chunks of 64 KiB); gunzip returns the bytes decoded so far on a truncated stream.
rows.failure_semantics: a stream cut short returns partial data silently: of 17 malformed gzip streams Scrapy returned data for 10, including a wrong CRC and a flipped bit that changed 2 bytes
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV asks for no compression and refuses an encoded body it did not ask for (UNSOLICITED_CONTENT_ENCODING); adapter/web/src/gzip.rs is a native bounded gunzip (CRC-32 and length verified, truncation an error) used for sitemaps
rows.knowledge: a bounded native inflate for the other content codings and for transfer compression: whether requesting gzip on page fetches saves enough bytes and time on real pages to justify sending Accept-Encoding, with the decoded size capped and the stored capture's hash defined (decoded bytes or received bytes)
rows.evidence: gzip decoder built and proven on 319 reference streams (tools/commerce/gzip_oracle.py, adapter/web/tests/gzip_oracle.rs), live: macrumors.com sitemap index 34 entries and note.com 10, matching Python's gunzip; 6 of 178 sites with sitemaps publish only .gz
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: partly answered: sitemaps done; page-transfer compression open

rows.behaviour: Links from <a> and <area> href (configurable tags and attrs), whitespace stripped, resolved against <base href>, URL made safe, deduplicated by canonical URL, rel=nofollow recorded; deny_extensions removes media, archive and document extensions; schemes limited; allow/deny regexes and domains.
rows.configuration: allow, deny, allow_domains, deny_domains, restrict_xpaths, tags, attrs, canonicalize, unique, deny_extensions, schemes
rows.ecdev_today: a[href] only, same host only, resolved against <base href> (found and fixed: it used the page URL), no extension filter, rel not recorded
rows.knowledge: On 7 real pages ECDEV and Scrapy agree except where recorded: Scrapy's extension filter would drop 26 same-host links, all Wikipedia 'File:*.jpg' description pages that are HTML, so ECDEV's content-type check after fetch is the safer rule; <area> and <base> occurred in 0 of 57 sampled pages.
rows.evidence: measurement in this wave (1,740 links); adapter/web/src/lib.rs test relative_links_resolve_against_base_href
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answered for extension filter and base; area and rel open on larger samples

rows.behaviour: allowed_domains becomes ^(.*\.)?(d1|d2)$; subdomains of an allowed domain follow; empty means everything.
rows.failure_semantics: filtered requests are counted by domain
rows.ecdev_today: links are kept only when their host equals the page's host
rows.knowledge: Of 1,740 real links 59 (3.4%) go to another host of the same registrable domain, almost all Wikipedia language editions and bbc.com help and shop sites: different sites in practice, so exact-host scope is a defensible default.

rows.behaviour: Depth is the parent's plus one (reset on request); DEPTH_LIMIT drops deeper requests; DEPTH_PRIORITY lowers priority by depth; URLLENGTH_LIMIT (2,083) drops longer URLs.
rows.ecdev_today: CrawlLimits.max_depth; priority ordering; found and fixed: no URL length bound, now MAX_URL_BYTES = 8,192 at canonicalisation
rows.knowledge: Measured on 2,611 page links and 646 post URLs the longest was 247 characters, so the bound limits abuse, never real links.

rows.behaviour: lxml iterparse in recover mode over url and sitemap elements; relative loc resolved against the sitemap URL; xhtml:link alternates optional; a gzip body (magic number) or an .xml/.xml.gz URL decoded under DOWNLOAD_MAXSIZE; robots Sitemap lines read bytewise.
rows.failure_semantics: malformed XML is recovered as far as it parses; an undecodable gzip returns None and warns
rows.ecdev_today: adapter/web/src/sitemap.rs: sitemaps.org limits (50,000 entries, 50 MiB), absolute http(s) locations only (others counted as rejected, never repaired), gzip decoded natively and refused whole on any error
rows.knowledge: Gap closed: compressed sitemaps were refused outright and 6 of 178 sites with sitemaps publish only those. Differences kept: no recover-mode XML, no relative locations, no alternates.
rows.evidence: adapter/web/tests/gzip_oracle.rs; live fetch of two gzip sitemaps
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: open sub-questions: xhtml:link alternates for multilingual products, recover-mode XML

rows.behaviour: Encoding from explicit argument, BOM, HTTP header, meta declaration, then statistical inference, default utf-8.
rows.ecdev_today: adapter/web/src/document.rs decodes under a declared charset or valid UTF-8 and refuses the rest, with no statistical guessing
rows.knowledge: Settled earlier by research/commerce/charset-benchmark.json: 44 of 48 pages on 19 Japanese retailers decoded; the 4 refusals were one stub with no product data.

rows.behaviour: Closes the crawl after a timeout, N items, N pages, N errors, N seconds or N pages without a new item.
rows.configuration: CLOSESPIDER_TIMEOUT, ITEMCOUNT, PAGECOUNT, ERRORCOUNT, TIMEOUT_NO_ITEM, PAGECOUNT_NO_ITEM
rows.ecdev_today: run budgets: max_pages, max_urls, max_depth, deadline; no yield-based stop
rows.knowledge: does stopping a crawl after N pages that surface no product save requests without losing products, on recorded crawls of real store sites
rows.evidence: no recorded product-yield crawl traces yet
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: open: needs per-page yield traces from live crawls

rows.behaviour: Per-request download_latency in meta; counters for retries, redirects, filtered requests.
rows.ecdev_today: headers now carry ttfb_ms and body_ms for each request and provider calls report content_ttfb_ms and content_body_ms beside the whole-source latency_ms
rows.knowledge: Observability the adaptive-delay question needs; live: 12 origins measured.

rows.behaviour: Graceful stop waits for in-flight requests; forced stop cancels them; the downloader stops accepting requests and cancels queued downloads.
rows.ecdev_today: frontier cancel(run) marks open URLs CANCELLED; the deadline does the same; leased work expires and is observable
rows.knowledge: Same intent; ECDEV's cancellation is a persisted state.

rows.donor_source: searched scrapy/ for private, loopback and link-local address checks: none outside the telnet console's bind address
rows.behaviour: Scrapy fetches whatever address a URL resolves to.
rows.ecdev_today: private, loopback, link-local and special addresses are refused after DNS resolution, and the connection is pinned to the checked address
rows.knowledge: A deliberate and proven divergence in ECDEV's favour for a crawler fed URLs from the open web.
rows.evidence: grep over the pinned source; adapter/web tests

native_changes: adapter/web/src/robots.rs: consecutive User-agent lines no longer erase a wildcard group (google.com's live robots.txt allowed /search); bare CR ends a line; rule priority is the pattern as written and the least restrictive of equal different patterns wins (monolog.r-n-i.jp, cs.android.com); one pattern given both directives stays refused

adapter/web/src/lib.rs: a raw non-ASCII Location is percent-encoded as received and followed instead of being dropped; <base href> resolves relative links; an unsolicited Content-Encoding is refused by name; a declared Content-Length past the 4 MiB cap is refused before reading; per-request ttfb_ms and body_ms recorded
adapter/web/src/gzip.rs and sitemap.rs: native bounded gzip decoder (CRC-32 and length verified, truncation an error); compressed sitemaps are read; .gz sitemap URLs pass the content-type gate
domain/commerce/src/research.rs: 408 retried, 501, 505 and 511 not retried; content request latency reported per call
domain/commerce/src/frontier.rs: URLs longer than 8,192 bytes have no identity (URL_TOO_LONG)

36-host survey through ecdev.research.run: 19 fetched, 0 sent an unsolicited Content-Encoding, the rest refused by robots or the AI-agent policy or unreachable

gzip sitemaps: macrumors.com 34 entries, note.com 10 entries, equal to Python's gunzip; suzuri.jp refuses AI agents and was not fetched

fixture_and_oracle_only: URL identity (569 rewrites), redirect decisions (2,000), robots (1,620 + 2,538), cache freshness (528), retry (500 statuses), gzip (319 streams): frozen donor or reference-implementation behaviour, never live
